newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA HOPES TO AWARD CELLPHONE LICENCES BY OCT.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA HOPES TO AWARD CELLPHONE LICENCES BY OCT.

text.p: The award of two licences to establish cellular telephone networks in Botswana will be made by early October, a Botswana Telecommunications Authority official said on Thursday.
"We are hoping to have evaluated the tenders in time for decisions by our Board on October 2," Claes Rosvall, consultant to the Botswana Telecommunications Authority said.
"If that is not possible, we will not wait for the next meeting (in November), but call a special one."

Five Botswana companies have submitted bids for the tender -- two with South Africa's Vodacom and MTN, one with partners from India and Mauritius, one with partners from Zimbabwe and Portugal and one with a partner from France.

Vodacom, which operates a network in South Africa, has formed a partnership with Botswana Telecommunications Corporation known as Botswana Vodacom Cellular (BVC), while MTN -- also a South African network operator -- had joined up with a Botswana-owned consortium Loapi Holdings.
Vodacom is partly owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc , while MTN is owned by Cable & Wireless Plc and others.
Portugal Telecom and Zimbabwe's TS Masiyiwa Holdings form part of the third bid and France Telecom together with a consortium of five Botswana companies part of the fourth bid.
The Mauritius and Indian companies which form part of the fifth bid have not been identified.
Botswana Vodacom Cellular (BVC) has promised that a cellphone network will be in place before the end of the year if it is succcesful in obtaining a licence.
Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig said he was confident the BVC consortium would be awarded a licence.
"I am 99.9 percent sure we will be granted a licence, I cannot imagine us not getting one," he said in Gaborone. "I expect to be using my cellphone in Botswana by Christmas."

BTC chief executive Olebile Gaborone said BVC planned to invest 61 million pula in the network. The company would be owned 40 percent each by BTC and Vodacom and the remaining 20 percent offered to the public, possibly within 12 months.
Knott-Craig said BVC's plan was to eventually cover every square metre of country by a satellite system.
Botswana covers 582,000 square kilometres, of which two thirds is covered by the Kalahari Desert, with a population of slightly less than 1.5 million.
The initial cellular market has been estimated by a BTC executive at around 10,000, rising over 10 years to between 50,000 and 60,000.
"It makes no sense to cover only one of the areas. BVC would initially give 61 percent coverage, but within three to five years, there would be nowhere in Botswana without service," Knott-Craig said.
